label: Mechanisms
description: Named processes, models, rules, and selection modes with their ordered logic — formulas and numbered conditions.

cards.definition: p² + 2pq + q² = 1. p² = freq(AA); 2pq = freq(Aa); q² = freq(aa); p+q=1 for a biallelic locus.
(1) No mutation, (2) no migration/gene flow, (3) infinite population (no drift), (4) no selection, (5) random mating. Violation of any one shifts allele or genotype frequencies away from HWE.
p = (2·N_AA + N_Aa) / (2·N_total). Each AA contributes 2 A alleles; each Aa contributes 1; each aa contributes 0. q = 1 − p.

cards.term: Carrier frequency for a rare recessive disease
cards.definition: If disease frequency is q², then q ≈ √(disease freq); carrier frequency ≈ 2pq. When q is small, carriers ≫ affected individuals.
Hemizygous males express recessive at frequency q (one X). Females express recessive at q². Disease prevalence in males = q; in females = q². Males affected at higher rate, ratio = 1/q.
Probability the two alleles at a locus are identical by descent. F=0 random mating; F=1 fully inbred. Genotype frequencies become p²+Fpq, 2pq(1−F), q²+Fpq.
Pooling subpopulations with different allele frequencies produces apparent excess of homozygotes vs HWE, even if each subpop is internally in HWE. Pooled heterozygosity = 2 p̄ q̄ − 2·Var(p).
V_P = V_A + V_D + V_I + V_E. Additive (predictably heritable) + dominance (same-locus) + epistatic (cross-locus) + environmental (not inherited). Selection acts on V_P; only V_A predictably evolves.
h² = V_A / V_P. Predicts response to selection. Estimated from parent-offspring regression slope.
H² = V_G / V_P = (V_A + V_D + V_I) / V_P. Total genetic share of phenotypic variance.
R = h² · S. Response to selection = narrow-sense heritability × selection differential. If h² = 0, R = 0 regardless of S.
S = mean trait value of breeders − mean trait value of original population. Measures intensity of selection.

(1) Heritable variation in a trait, (2) differential survival or reproduction based on the trait, (3) consequent fitness differences across generations. All three required; remove any one and adaptation stops.

Obs 1: heritable variation exists. Obs 2: more offspring produced than survive. Obs 3: survival/reproduction is non-random. Inference: heritable variants that raise reproduction become more common — natural selection.
Selection dominates when |s| ≫ 1/(2Ne); drift dominates when |s| ≪ 1/(2Ne). For diploids, threshold ≈ 1/(2Ne). Large N → even weak selection beats drift; small N → drift overrides moderate selection.

DIRECTIONAL: mean shifts toward favored extreme; variance often decreases. STABILIZING: mean unchanged; extremes pruned; variance shrinks. DISRUPTIVE: extremes favored; variance increases; can produce bimodal distribution.
rB > C. Altruism is favored when relatedness × benefit to recipient > cost to actor. r = relatedness coefficient, B = benefit (in offspring units), C = cost.
Identical twins r=1.0; parent-offspring r=0.5; full sib r=0.5; half-sib r=0.25; first cousin r=0.125; hymenopteran sisters (haplodiploid) r=0.75.
Direct fitness (own offspring) + indirect fitness (extra offspring of relatives, weighted by r). Captures genetic contribution at the allele level, not the individual level.
A strategy that, once common, cannot be invaded by any rare alternative. Frequency-dependent Nash equilibrium for evolutionary games.
When V<C: mixed ESS at p_Hawk* = V/C. When V≥C: pure-Hawk ESS (no mixed equilibrium; Doves can't invade).
Hawk vs Hawk: ½(V−C) each. Hawk vs Dove: V (Hawk takes), 0 (Dove flees). Dove vs Dove: V/2 each.
Asexual female passes 100% of her genes; sexual female passes 50% (half from male). Per-offspring transmission halved — sex must produce ≥2× the benefit to break even.

(1) MUTATION ACCUMULATION (Medawar): late-life deleterious mutations escape selection. (2) ANTAGONISTIC PLEIOTROPY (Williams): allele helps young, hurts old; net favored. (3) DISPOSABLE SOMA (Kirkwood): maintenance vs reproduction trade-off.

TEMPORAL (different breeding times), BEHAVIORAL (different courtship signals), MECHANICAL (incompatible genitalia/flowers), GAMETIC (sperm/pollen don't fertilize), HABITAT (don't meet because of niche).
HYBRID INVIABILITY (zygote/embryo fails). HYBRID STERILITY (mules — develops but can't reproduce). HYBRID BREAKDOWN (F1 fine but F2/backcross weak).
ALLOPATRIC (full barrier, no gene flow), PERIPATRIC (small founder pop isolated), PARAPATRIC (partial separation, ongoing gene flow), SYMPATRIC (same range, niche shift or polyploidy).
Selection STRENGTHENS prezygotic isolation in zones of secondary contact when hybrids are unfit. Signature: greater prezygotic divergence in sympatry than allopatry.

Mechanism for postzygotic isolation. Independently evolved alleles in two populations are individually fine but negative-epistatic when combined. F1 buffered (heterozygous); F2 exposes incompatible homozygous combinations → hybrid breakdown.

Standing species count S* = balance between immigration (declines as island fills) and extinction (rises with more species). S* depends on island size (extinction) and distance from source (immigration). Equilibrium is dynamic — turnover continues at S*.

Coevolution intensity varies across the range — HOTSPOTS (intense reciprocal selection) + COLDSPOTS (weak/none). Gene flow + local trait evolution → mosaic of coevolutionary states; trait mismatch is positive evidence of dynamic process.

Optimal pathogen virulence depends on transmission mode. Direct/respiratory: low virulence favored (need mobile host). Vector- or water-borne: high virulence tolerated (host immobility doesn't break transmission).
Sex (recombination) is favored because parasites coevolve rapidly; new allele combinations help hosts stay one step ahead. Named for Lewis Carroll's queen who must run to stay in place.
Asexual lineages cannot purge slightly deleterious mutations efficiently — mutations accumulate one-way (the ratchet clicks but never unclicks) → mutational meltdown over time.

Arbitrary female preference + heritable male trait → offspring inherit BOTH preference and trait → preferred trait amplifies generationally even if costly. Self-reinforcing loop until natural-selection cost balances sexual-selection benefit.
Heterozygote has higher fitness than either homozygote. Maintains BOTH alleles in the population at a stable polymorphism. Equilibrium q* = (1−w_AA)/((1−w_AA) + (1−w_aa)) using fitness deficits.
Fitness of a phenotype DECREASES as it becomes more common; rare types are favored. Maintains polymorphism (e.g., side-blotched lizards rock-paper-scissors; MHC alleles).
Rapid diversification of one lineage into many ecologically distinct species. Conditions: (1) open niches (post-extinction or new habitat), (2) key innovation, (3) ecological opportunity.

Eukaryotes acquired organelles by engulfing free-living bacteria. Mitochondria from alphaproteobacteria (~2.0–1.6 GYA, eukaryotic stem). Chloroplasts from cyanobacteria (~1.5 GYA, Archaeplastida only — happened in cells that already had mitochondria).

(1) CONVERGENCE: similar traits evolve independently from different ancestral states. (2) PARALLELISM: similar derived states from the same ancestral state in separate lineages. (3) REVERSAL: derived state reverts to ancestral.

MONOPHYLETIC (clade): ancestor + ALL descendants — only valid group. PARAPHYLETIC: ancestor + SOME descendants (excludes some). POLYPHYLETIC: members lacking shared immediate ancestor (built on convergence).
Among candidate trees, prefer the tree requiring the FEWEST evolutionary changes. Assumes evolution is rare. Fails for fast-evolving sequences (long-branch attraction).
(1) Light-sensitive patch (photoreceptors). (2) Cupped patch — directional sensitivity. (3) Pinhole eye (Nautilus) — image without lens. (4) Lensed eye — sharp focus via co-opted crystallins.

Modern Homo sapiens originated in Africa ~300 KYA. Major out-of-Africa wave ~70 KYA met Neanderthals in the Middle East/Europe. Interbreeding ~50–60 KYA left ~1–4% Neanderthal DNA in non-Africans, ~0% in sub-Saharan Africans.
End-Ordovician (~445 MYA), Late Devonian (~375 MYA), end-Permian (~252 MYA, largest, ~95% marine), end-Triassic (~201 MYA), end-Cretaceous (K-Pg, ~66 MYA, dinosaurs).
Use ≥2 drugs simultaneously so pathogen needs multiple independent resistance mutations. Probability of double resistance ≈ p₁ × p₂ ≈ 10⁻⁹ × 10⁻⁹ = 10⁻¹⁸ vs 10⁻⁹ for single drug.
